answer: Reputation-weighted rate throttling. Each identity draws service from a shared inlet whose throughput is capped by cumulative reputation, so fresh identities start at a slow trickle. To flood the river of requests, an attacker must sustain many identities over time, paying continuous compute and fee costs per identity that scale with elapsed history rather than a one-time deposit, and every harbor of capacity they occupy is reclaimed when reputation decays from inactivity.
